rendered: The premise is not supported. The document does not show bare Al outperforming carbon/Al at the highest current tested. It reports the opposite. Carbon/Al kept a low voltage hysteresis even at high currents, the paper stating that the carbon nucleation layer enables a low hysteresis, with a[1] 45 mV[2] hysteresis at 4 mA/cm^2[3]. Bare Al, by contrast, was prone to failure at these currents.[4] In the cycling comparison, the bare Al electrode showed signs of shorting, attributed to uneven plating from its higher nucleation overpotential, and delamination failures that did not occur on carbon/Al. The carbon nucleation layer, providing a[5][6] three-dimensional interface[7], is credited with the more stable plating. The document gives no hysteresis value for bare Al at the highest current, so no difference can be calculated. The only hysteresis comparison at that current is to earlier work using Cu electrodes, which reported nearly double the hysteresis[8] at that current; that is not bare Al.
